inspectedText: The NPS account presents the 1848 escape with Ellen passing as a sick white male slaveholder and William as the enslaved attendant. It explains the sling as a solution to signing, bandages to facial appearance, and apparent hearing trouble to unwanted conversation. Charleston and Baltimore passages describe obstacles and interventions rather than a foolproof disguise. It distinguishes reaching Philadelphia and settling in Boston from later 1850 danger and flight to England. The footnotes cite the 1860 narrative and additional scholarship/period records. Many detailed journey scenes therefore are not independent eyewitness corroboration. A map label's December25–January1848 is internally awkward; exact dates require later reconciliation.
sourceQualityRationale: National historical-site institutional synthesis with claim-level footnotes; credible historiography and pointers to primary records, substantially derivative of Craft for journey particulars.
